newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE COACH ASKS MARADONA TO FINANCE TEAM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE COACH ASKS MARADONA TO FINANCE TEAM.

text.p: Former Argentine international Mario Kempes has asked Diego Maradona and Argentina manager Daniel Passarella to help support Lushnje, the troubled Albanian first division side he coaches, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

Sporti Shqiptar, the Balkan country's main sports newspaper, said Kempes had sought financial support from his two compatriots. Passarella was captain and Kempes leading striker of the Argentina side which won the 1978 World Cup on home soil.
"(Kempes) asked Maradona and Passarella to provide financial support for our team," Lushnje's assistant coach Hasan Lika told the newspaper.

The club is in financial difficulty after the arrest of its president, Pellumb Xhaferri, whose father owned one of several pyramid investment schemes which have collapsed with the life savings of hundreds of thousands of investors.

Kempes left Albania after protesters demanding refunds set fire to buildings in Lushnje and other towns. The club's two Brazilian players, Carlos Eduardo Castro de Souza and Valdemir Souza dos Santos also left but Nigerian midfielder Leonardo Ineh Nosa stayed behind.

Kempes signed a two-year contract worth $350,000 with Lushnje, the first club in Europe's poorest country to sign foreign players. Authorities have arrested about 150 people and banned all sports events to prevent new outbreaks of violence.
